name: Pregnancy danger signs
tagline: Bleeding, severe pain, no movement — when to go in.
sources: South African Society of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists

urgent.heading: Go to hospital now if
urgent.primary_message: Pregnancy danger signs can mean the difference between life and death — for mother or baby. Don't wait. Don't second-guess. Go.
red_flags: Heavy bleeding from the vagina — more than a normal period
Severe abdominal or back pain that won't ease
Severe headache with blurred vision or seeing spots
Sudden severe swelling of face, hands, or feet
Baby not moving as usual (after 28 weeks)

what_is_it.heading: Why this matters
what_is_it.lede: Pregnancy is generally safe in South Africa, but maternal deaths are still too common — and most are preventable. Knowing the danger signs and acting fast saves lives.
paragraphs: South Africa records over 1,000 maternal deaths every year. The Saving Mothers report shows that most happen from preventable causes — bleeding, high blood pressure, infection, complications of pre-existing conditions. Many deaths happen because warning signs were dismissed or care was delayed.

You don't need to know what's wrong. You just need to recognise that something is wrong, and get to a hospital. Free obstetric care is available at every government hospital. Trust your instinct — if something feels wrong, it probably is.

items.body: South African women die in pregnancy or childbirth every year. The vast majority of these deaths are preventable.

items.headline: MomConnect
items.body: Free WhatsApp pregnancy support from NDoH in all SA languages. Send 'Hi' to 079 631 2456 to register.

items.headline: Free care
items.body: All antenatal visits, birth, and emergency obstetric care are free at every government hospital and clinic.

items.headline: Trust yourself
items.body: If something feels wrong, go in. Healthcare workers would rather see you for nothing than miss something serious.

pull_quote.text: Every maternal death has a story behind it of warning signs missed or dismissed. If you are pregnant and worried, the right answer is always to be checked. Always.

signs.heading: Warning signs by stage of pregnancy
signs.lede: Some signs matter at any stage. Others matter more at certain times. When in doubt — get checked.

items.title: First 12 weeks
items.description: Heavy bleeding, severe one-sided pain (could be ectopic pregnancy — life-threatening), severe vomiting that prevents keeping fluids down, fever above 38°C.

items.title: After 12 weeks
items.description: Heavy bleeding, severe headache with vision changes (possible pre-eclampsia), severe swelling, baby movements slowing or stopping (after 28 weeks).

items.title: Near or at term (after 37 weeks)
items.description: Regular contractions, water breaking, bleeding, reduced fetal movement, severe headache or stomach pain. Don't try to time things at home — go in.

items.title: If a danger sign appears — go to hospital
items.description: Don't drive yourself if you can avoid it. Call an ambulance or have someone drive you. Take your antenatal card or clinic book.

items.title: Don't try to time symptoms at home
items.description: Severe pain, bleeding, or vision changes don't need timing. Go in. Pre-eclampsia and ectopic pregnancy can kill within hours.

items.title: Go to your booked hospital or the nearest one
items.description: Government hospitals must accept pregnant emergencies regardless of where you booked. Take your records if you have them.

items.title: If unsure — message MomConnect
items.description: Free WhatsApp support — send 'Hi' to 079 631 2456. Your clinic can also advise whether to come in. When unsure, choose hospital.

items.title: Attend every antenatal visit
items.description: Most danger signs are caught early at routine antenatal visits. Free at every clinic. The schedule prevents emergencies.

get_help.heading: Where to go
get_help.lede: Pregnancy emergencies need hospital, not clinic. Go to a government hospital with obstetric services — Tygerberg, Charlotte Maxeke, Steve Biko, King Edward, and others around the country.

helplines.name: Emergency (mobile)
helplines.description: Reaches any emergency service from a cellphone

helplines.description: Free pregnancy support and advice via WhatsApp
